details:
I want to provide feedback regarding my experience with moderation and enforcement in VRChat.

One of the biggest frustrations is the inconsistency in how rules appear to be enforced. The policies around prints and image content feel extremely vague, which makes it difficult for users to know what is actually allowed versus what may suddenly result in punishment. Many suspensions seem to happen without clear explanations or examples, leaving users confused rather than educated on what needs to change.

At the same time, there are serious issues within the community that often feel ignored or under-addressed. Users regularly encounter sexual harassment, targeted hate toward transgender people, and harassment toward LGBTQ+ members, yet these behaviors frequently appear to continue openly without visible moderation action. From a community perspective, it can feel discouraging to see ambiguous content rules enforced more aggressively than direct harmful behavior toward real people.

Moderation systems work best when rules are transparent, consistently enforced, and focused on protecting users from genuine harm. Right now, the imbalance creates a perception that cosmetic or unclear violations are prioritized over player safety and harassment concerns.

I believe many users would appreciate:

Clearer definitions and examples regarding print/image content rules.

Better communication when actions are taken against accounts.

More visible enforcement against harassment, hate speech, stalking, and discrimination.

Faster responses to reports involving targeted abuse or unsafe behavior.

Consistent standards applied equally across the platform.

This feedback is not meant as an attack on moderators individually. I understand moderation at scale is difficult. However, many users feel unheard when serious reports go unanswered while vague policy enforcement results in suspensions without meaningful explanation.

I hope the moderation team and platform leadership take community concerns seriously and continue improving transparency, fairness, and user safety moving forward.
title: Lack of support
